record.context_brief: Tensor-product cancellation up to elementary equivalence
record.original_question: Let N_1,N_2,M_1,M_2 be separable II_1 factors such that N_1^U ⊗ N_2^U ≅ M_1^U ⊗ M_2^U. Must the factors match up, up to permuting indices, at the level of elementary equivalence; that is, after a permutation, is N_i elementarily equivalent to M_i for each i?

evidence.quote: Problem 49. Suppose N1, N2, M1, M2 are separable II1 factors such that NU1 ⊗NU2 ∼= MU1 ⊗MU2, then is Ni elementarily equivalent to Mi up to permutation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N_1, N_2, M_1, M_2$ be separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. For a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $P$ with separable predual and faithful normal trace $\tau_P$, let $P^{\mathcal{U}}$ denote its tracial ultrapower with respect to a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, that is, the quotient $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N},P)/\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{U}}$ where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{U}}=\{(x_n)_n : \lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}}\tau_P(x_n^*x_n)=0\}$, equipped with its canonical tracial von Neumann algebra structure. Two tracial von Neumann algebras are called elementarily equivalent if they have the same first-order theory in the continuous logic of tracial von Neumann algebras (equivalently, by the Keisler–Shelah theorem in the continuous setting, if they have isomorphic ultrapowers with respect to some ultrafilter).

Suppose that
$$ N_1^{\mathcal{U}} \,\overline{\otimes}\, N_2^{\mathcal{U}} \;\cong\; M_1^{\mathcal{U}} \,\overline{\otimes}\, M_2^{\mathcal{U}} $$
as tracial von Neumann algebras. Must there exist a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,2\}$ such that $N_i$ is elementarily equivalent to $M_{\sigma(i)}$ for $i=1,2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of a recent compilation of fifty open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors (2025). Web search reveals active research on elementary equivalence of II_1 factors and tensor-product behaviour, but no published resolution of this particular tensor-cancellation-up-to-elementary-equivalence problem. It appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Elementary equivalence and disintegration of tracial von Neumann algebras
status_evidence.snippet: An analog of the disintegration theorem for tracial von Neumann algebras was proved in the setting of elementary equivalence rather than isomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on elementary equivalence of tracial von Neumann algebras; no resolution of the stated tensor-cancellation question.

status_evidence.title: An exotic II_1 factor without property Gamma
status_evidence.snippet: First explicit example of two non-elementarily equivalent II_1 factors without property Gamma.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on distinguishing II_1 factors by elementary equivalence, but no statement settling tensor-product cancellation up to elementary equivalence.
